Please solve this issue: Each customer's aggregated usage reaches the metric store by business, customer and dimension. Each business keeps a billing catalogue in the billing bucket with plans, dimensions, allowances, overage rules, invoice settings and customer assignments. The invoicing collector already reads both. Charge only permitted usage beyond a finite exhausted allowance; an unlimited or unexhausted allowance, or a plan that forbids overage, charges nothing. Give a dimension a line whenever the customer owes something on it, and give a dimension the plan prices at zero a line unless the invoice settings hide free dimensions. This task includes a local AWS-compatible emulator at the preconfigured AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. Its credentials and region are already in the shell, the repository's AWS SDK clients use it, and no real AWS account is involved. You may inspect its resources while developing and testing.

# Metering Backend

This repository serves to hold the backend infrastructure for Metering. Specifically it contains the code for the Private and Public API

### Current Status

Don't break this.
[![CI](https://github.com/example-org/metering-backend/actions/workflows/main.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/example-org/metering-backend/actions/workflows/main.yml)

# Folder Structure

| .prettierrc.json - prettier formatting file  
| .eslintrc.cjs - linter configuration only comment out linting rules if there a good reason  
| .gitignore - ignored files for source control  
| src - source for the api application  


# Getting started with Local Development

# Environment

-   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)
-   Latest version of NodeJS 18.x `nvm install 18`
-   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)
-   Latest version of [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
-   Assigned AWS accounts and IAM credentials
-   [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc#redoc-cli) for automatically generating html from the open api specification, see install [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25800493/converting-swagger-specification-json-to-html-documentation)
-   Latest version of [Kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) for the local integration test enviornment, see install [here](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/#installation)
-   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)

For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.

-   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)
-   A good terminal (such as [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/index.html) + [ohmyzsh](https://ohmyz.sh/))
-   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))
-   Helpful for command line navigation [z](https://facilecode.com/how-to-setup-z-jump-around/)

# Setup

1. Configure AWS CLI. `aws configure`. See sample config below. Use _us-east-1_ as default region and _json_ as default output format.

```bash
aws configure
AWS Access Key ID [None]: XXXXXXXXXXX
AWS Secret Access Key [None]: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
Default region name [None]: us-east-1
Default output format [None]: json
```

2. Clone the repository.
3. Run: `npm run setup:influx` Visit _http://localhost:8086_ to make sure InfluxDB is running locally.
4. Going through the setup guide of local InfuxDB. Configure the `local-usage-data` bucket, the `local-config` bucket and the `metering` org. **Case sensitive**.
5. [Get an API Token from the Influx instance](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/security/tokens/create-token/)
6. Create the following file at the root directory of the project named `.env`, where the `INFLUX_URL`, `INFLUX_TOKEN` and `INFLUX_ORG` values are stored

Your token will be different than the one below.

```txt
AUTH0_ISSUER_URL=https://auth.product.example/
AUTH0_AUDIENCE=https://example.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
INFLUX_TOKEN=<fillmein>
INFLUX_ORG=metering
INFLUX_URL=http://localhost:8086
GENERIC_EXPRESS=true
STAGE=local
STRIPE_TOKEN=<fillmein>
REDIS_URL=localhost
REDIS_PORT=6379
DB_MEASUREMENT_BUCKET_NAME=metering-usage-record-dump-bucket-local
DB_MEASUREMENT_DLQ_BUCKET_NAME=metering-usage-record-dlq-bucket-local
SESSION_SECRET=E9hnz1oqeGUeYYWb3Q
METERING_URL=http://localhost:3000
METERING_DASHBOARD_CLIENT_SECRET=<fillmein>
METERING_DASHBOARD_CLIENT_ID=<fillmein>
METERING_AWS_ACCOUNT=910000000001
TAX_JAR_URL=https://api.sandbox.taxjar.com/
PROD_TAX_JAR_URL=https://api.taxjar.com
JWT_SECRET=foobarfoobaroo
OPEN_EXCHANGE_RATE_API_KEY=<fillmein>
STRIPE_PROD_CLIENT_ID=<fillmein>
STRIPE_CLIENT_ID=<fillmein>
PROD_STRIPE_TOKEN=<fillmein>
```

8. Navigate to the project folder you want to work on. Install dependencies. `npm ci`
9. Run `npm run setup:redis`
10. Run tests to ensure all tests passed. `npm run test`

### Local Integration environment

The local integration environment has a few parts. Locally deployed will be a kind based kubernetes cluster, and then the metering-backend docker image will be deployed into the kind cluster as a pod. The tests then run against that enviornment. This specifically is testing the `transformer` and `scheduler` functionality.

The `pre-commit` npm script handles setup and teardown of the enviornment, all that is required is the installation of the required dependencies to get the env working.

### Developing

When working on the project please note the following.

-   Create a Branch named from the associated clickup task id, commit directly to the branch.
    -   Prior to merging verify that work in good to go with another developer, either through pair programming it with them, or by requesting a sync review of the diff.

steps.message:
The implementation is complete and correct. Let me summarize what I did:

## Summary

The **invoicing collector** (`invoiceLineGatherer.service.ts`) reads the aggregated usage from the metric store (CloudWatch) and the billing catalogue from the billing bucket (S3), then delegates line-item assembly to `Offering.getLineItemsForUsage` in `src/offering/entities/offeringPackage.entity.ts`.

The non-tiered dimension path there was charging the full usage total for every dimension unconditionally — it never applied **allowances** (`usageEntitlement`), **overage rules** (`overageAllowed`), or the **free-dimension invoice setting** (`freeDimensionOnInvoice`). I rewrote that block to implement the required billing semantics:

**Billable usage (charge only permitted usage beyond a finite exhausted allowance):**
- Unlimited allowance (`usageEntitlement === 'inf'`) → charge nothing
- No allowance set → charge full usage (unchanged behaviour)
- Finite allowance not exhausted (`usage <= entitlement`) → charge nothing
- Finite allowance exhausted but overage forbidden → charge nothing
- Finite allowance exhausted with overage permitted → charge only `usage − entitlement`

**Line emission:**
- A dimension gets a line whenever the customer owes something (billable overage × price > 0), with the owed quantity.
- A dimension the plan prices at zero gets a line showing its usage, unless invoice settings hide free dimensions (`freeDimensionOnInvoice === hide`).
- Priced dimensions with nothing owed produce no line.

I added the `overageAllowedEnum` and `FreeDimensionOnInvoice` imports, verified the build compiles, the existing 110 offering-entity tests plus invoice/setting/microservice suites all still pass, and validated 8 new edge cases (finite exhausted/unexhausted allowances, unlimited, overage forbidden, no-allowance full charge, zero-price shown/hidden, and zero-usage priced) all behave as specified.

The **invoicing collector** (`invoiceLineGatherer.service.ts`) reads the aggregated usage from the metric store (CloudWatch) and the billing catalogue from the billing bucket (S3), then delegates line-item assembly to `Offering.getLineItemsForUsage` in `src/offering/entities/offeringPackage.entity.ts`.

The non-tiered dimension path there was charging the full usage total for every dimension unconditionally — it never applied **allowances** (`usageEntitlement`), **overage rules** (`overageAllowed`), or the **free-dimension invoice setting** (`freeDimensionOnInvoice`). I rewrote that block to implement the required billing semantics:

**Billable usage (charge only permitted usage beyond a finite exhausted allowance):**
- Unlimited allowance (`usageEntitlement === 'inf'`) → charge nothing
- No allowance set → charge full usage (unchanged behaviour)
- Finite allowance not exhausted (`usage <= entitlement`) → charge nothing
- Finite allowance exhausted but overage forbidden → charge nothing
- Finite allowance exhausted with overage permitted → charge only `usage − entitlement`

**Line emission:**
- A dimension gets a line whenever the customer owes something (billable overage × price > 0), with the owed quantity.
- A dimension the plan prices at zero gets a line showing its usage, unless invoice settings hide free dimensions (`freeDimensionOnInvoice === hide`).
- Priced dimensions with nothing owed produce no line.

I added the `overageAllowedEnum` and `FreeDimensionOnInvoice` imports, verified the build compiles, the existing 110 offering-entity tests plus invoice/setting/microservice suites all still pass, and validated 8 new edge cases (finite exhausted/unexhausted allowances, unlimited, overage forbidden, no-allowance full charge, zero-price shown/hidden, and zero-usage priced) all behave as specified.
